name: New Blood
oracle_text:
As an additional cost to cast this spell, tap an untapped Vampire you control.
Gain control of target creature. Change the text of that creature by replacing all instances of one creature type with Vampire.
blocked_sentences: Change the text of that creature by replacing all instances of one creature type with Vampire.

needs.what: A text-changing effect (613.1c, layer 3) as an op: point it at one object, have its controller name a creature type, and from then on every instance of that word on that object reads as Vampire -- its printed subtype line *and* the word wherever it appears inside its own rules text ("other Goblins you control get +1/+0", "{T}: Target Goblin gains haste", "Goblin creature you control"). Scoped from a survey of the engine while its three sibling capabilities were built, the two seams are already there and named: (1) the *choice* has no home on the source -- `choose_type` writes `chosen_type` onto `ctx.source_oid`, which for a sorcery is the spell on its way to the graveyard -- so it needs a field on the **target**, e.g. `GameObject.text_change = (from_type, to_type)`, which is also the right home because this is a continuous effect on that object; (2) the substitution itself needs two readers, `characteristics._compute` for the subtype line and `characteristics.abilities_of` for the rules text. `abilities_of` is the correct seam and already exists for `lose_all_abilities`, but the work there is the real cost: `Ability` is a **compiled** tree (`TriggerSpec`, `Cost`, static `affects` filters, effect dicts, `create_token` subtype lists, value selectors), so a substitution means rebuilding that tree with every subtype-bearing key rewritten, and getting the key list wrong in either direction is silent -- a missed key leaves the stolen lord pumping its old tribe, an over-eager one rewrites something that was never a creature type. It also needs a caching and acyclicity story, because `abilities_of` feeds `_battlefield_statics` which feeds `chars`. Olivia Voldaren's kin all hang on it: New Blood, Artificial Evolution, Mind Bend, Sleight of Mind, Glamerdye, Trickery Charm.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `add_subtype` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_characteristics.py:29, primitive at src/automtg/engine/primitives.py:851) is explicitly and only additive -- its docstring says "Types are always *added*" and `add_subtypes` unions onto `obj.added_subtypes` with no removal path -- so it would leave the old creature type in place, and "replacing all instances" is a substitution, not an addition. The `set_types` static (applied at src/automtg/engine/characteristics.py:230) is the only thing that ever takes a subtype away, and it does so as a side effect of dropping a whole *card* type (205.1b): it rewrites `types` wholesale from a fixed printed list and cannot be told "swap Goblin for Vampire while leaving Creature alone", nor can a static's magnitude be a type chosen at resolution. `animate` likewise assigns a fixed type line written on the card. `choose_type` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_control.py:136) can ask the question but not act on the answer: it writes `obj.chosen_type` onto `ctx.source_oid`, which for a sorcery is the spell itself on its way to the graveyard, and the only consumer is `{"chosen_type_of": "self"}` inside the *same* permanent's own abilities. Most decisively, the characteristics pipeline in src/automtg/engine/characteristics.py has no layer-3 step at all -- it goes straight from copy effects to type grants -- so nothing anywhere reads or rewrites the words inside another object's printed ability text; a permanent's abilities are matched by their authored spec, not by a mutable text. Approximating with `add_subtype` ("it's also a Vampire") is a different card: it would not stop the creature answering to its original type for anthems, fetches and tribal removal, and it would not touch the creature's own text, which is the half of New Blood that turns an opposing lord into yours. Re-checked after `skip_draw_step`, `delay.your_turn` and `look_at_top`'s `as`/`face_down` were added for Necropotence: none of the three helps here, and the characteristics pipeline still has no layer-3 step -- it goes straight from copy effects to type grants. This is the one capability of the four that is a rules subsystem rather than an op, which is why it was left rather than started inside a card-unblocking run.
